blurb:
Lucie is fifteen months old and just under eight pounds, which puts her right in that sweet spot between kitten and fully settled adult cat. Old enough that she's done with the knock-everything-off-the-counter phase. Young enough that she's still got plenty of good years ahead of her.

She's litter box trained, vaccinated, spayed, microchipped, and flea-treated. Her background before the shelter is thin, so compatibility with other animals and kids is listed as unknown. That's pretty normal for young cats who came in without much history attached. The staff at Lewisville can tell you more about what she's been like day to day at the shelter, so ask them when you visit.

Lucie is a domestic shorthair mix, easy to groom, straightforward to care for. If you've been thinking about adding a cat to the house and want one who's already past the most chaotic stage but still has tons of energy and personality ahead of her, she's worth a look. Swing by during visiting hours and ask for Lucie.
shelter_hours: Contact shelter for current visiting hours
scoring_notes:
• Fully ready to go home — spayed, vaccinated, microchipped, and at the ideal age for a first-time cat owner
• Backstory is thin and unremarkable, making her the least distinctive candidate for newsletter storytelling
• No urgency or long-wait indicators present; blurb reads as a fresh or recent intake

blurb:
Glynnis is eight years old, about 41 pounds, and has apparently been melting people at Mostly Mutts since the day she arrived from animal control. The volunteers call her sweet and precious. Her foster family called her the sweetest dog ever. She completed the Prison Pups training program. She alerts when someone comes to the door. And when she's deep in a nap, she makes little noises and kicks her feet around. She's been in foster homes, loved every minute of it, and she's ready for the real thing.

She does best in a quieter setting. The apartment foster situation didn't work well for her — too many people and dogs moving through tight spaces. She'd do much better in a house with a yard and some breathing room. Cats are a no-go; she went after one in a foster home. Other dogs are possible, but she needs a slow introduction and does best as an only dog. Kids ten and up are a good fit based on her history.

She's not looking for adventure. She's looking for a couch, someone to scratch her ears, and a front door to guard. If that sounds like your house, she'd probably fit right in.

Mostly Mutts is in Marietta. Submit an inquiry on their website and set up a time to meet Glynnis in person.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• At eight years old with multiple foster placements behind her, she almost certainly has the longest shelter journey of any candidate — strong urgency case
• Dreaming-dog detail (little noises, kicking feet mid-nap) is the kind of single image that sticks with newsletter readers and drives shares
• Stacked placement restrictions (no cats, slow dog intros, house with yard required) make her a harder adoption, but the right framing turns that into a targeted, high-impact call to action

blurb:
Eugene had a home. A real one, for about a year, with someone who clearly loved him. Then that person had to leave the country and couldn't take him along. So now Eugene is back at Mostly Mutts, adjusting to shelter life again, and looking for somebody patient enough to let him get there at his own pace.

He's a six-year-old Chihuahua mix, about 17 pounds, and the volunteers describe him as a sweet lap dog once he warms up. And he does warm up — he just needs time and a calm environment to get there. He's not a dog who's going to greet you at the door on day one. He's a dog who, after a few weeks of gentle consistency, is going to be glued to your side on the couch.

He's had some challenges with leashing and harnessing, so the right family will be comfortable reading his signals and not rushing the process. He did best as an only dog in his previous home, though he's shown no aggression toward other dogs at the shelter. Kids 15 and up who know how to give a dog space would be a good fit. He was fine with a cat in his last home, too.

If you've got a quiet household and you're the kind of person who appreciates a dog that chooses you deliberately, Eugene is worth meeting. Head to mostlymutts.org to submit an inquiry.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• His backstory — loved, lost his person to an international move, starting over — is the most emotionally resonant of the entire group
• Narrower placement profile (only dog, older kids, patient owner) limits adoptability but makes the right match feel meaningful and specific
• Returning to shelter life after a year in a real home signals genuine waiting-time urgency and rewards a newsletter audience that values second-chance stories

blurb:
Wilson came from animal control, went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, and is currently living it up in a foster home. He's three years old, about 46 pounds of Bulldog-Boxer mix, and his whole vibe is just... happy. Genuinely, enthusiastically, can't-help-himself happy.

The volunteers use him to help other dogs learn how to play. That's how good he is with other dogs. He talks while he plays — not barking, just making noise because he's having a great time and wants you to know it. During his bath at the shelter, he drank water straight from the sprayer and then handed out kisses. That's Wilson.

He does have a prey drive toward squirrels and small animals on walks, so cats are a hard no. But he's done great with kids of various ages and was friendly with the neighbor's chihuahua in his foster home. Toddlers are the one exception — not aggression, just a big excited guy who might accidentally knock a small kid over. If you've got older kids, a dog-friendly household, and room for a chatty, affectionate, goofy boy who graduated from an immersive training program, Wilson is worth a visit.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. Submit an inquiry on their website and plan to meet him in person to get the process started.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Prison Pups graduate who now teaches other dogs how to play — a built-in feel-good headline that writes itself
• Vivid, personality-packed details (sprayer kisses, play-by-play commentary) make him the most memorable candidate for reader engagement
• Animal-control origins plus program completion time suggest a meaningful shelter journey, adding adoption urgency without desperation

shelter_name: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue & Adoption, Inc.
blurb:
Turk came into Mostly Mutts as a kitten who needed a home. He's four months old, about 3.5 pounds, and already has everything handled on the medical side. Vaccines, microchip, neuter. All done.

He's described as sweet, active, and fun, and the listing makes a point of saying he's got cuddles for everyone. He plays with toys and then comes looking for you afterward. He does great with his siblings, so if you have a cat at home who'd enjoy a playmate, he's worth considering. Dogs are unknown, so bring yours in for a meet and greet if that's relevant.

The adoption fee is $175. Mostly Mutts operates out of Kennesaw, just a short drive from East Cobb. Get in touch at adopt@mostlymutts.org or call to schedule a visit and meet him in person.
scoring_notes:
• Fully vetted, playful, and affectionate — a genuinely easy adoption for the right household
• Blurb reads nearly identically to JD's, limiting standalone newsletter appeal and reader differentiation
• No distinctive backstory or wait-time signal makes him the weakest feature candidate of the group despite being a strong adoptee

shelter_name: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue & Adoption, Inc.
blurb:
Four months old, 3.5 pounds, and apparently named after a character from Scrubs. JD came into Mostly Mutts as a young kitten who needed somewhere to land. He got there, got healthy, and now he's ready to actually go home.

He's litter trained, up to date on vaccines, microchipped, and already neutered. The basics are handled. What you get is a kitten who plays hard with toys and then pivots immediately to wanting cuddles. He gets along great with his siblings, so if you've got another cat at home who could use some company, he's probably going to fit right in. Dogs are unknown, so a meet and greet would be a good idea if you've got one.

The adoption fee is $175. Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw, so not far at all from East Cobb. Email them at adopt@mostlymutts.org or give them a call to set up a visit.
scoring_notes:
• Turnkey adoption: vaccines, microchip, and neuter already done at a clear $175 price point — lowest friction of any candidate
• Play-hard-then-cuddle personality is broadly appealing and easy to visualize for newsletter readers
• Recently arrived young kitten with a thin backstory; limited urgency and minimal wait time reduce feature priority

shelter_name: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue & Adoption, Inc.
blurb:
She was found outside with a litter of kittens in someone's backyard, doing her best to keep her little family together. A foster family brought them all in, almost every kitten has found a home, and now it's Bernadette's turn. She's about a year old, roughly 7.5 pounds, and her foster describes her as "a beautiful kitty with a gentle soul and so much love to give." That's not just nice words. It matches.

She's a little shy when you first meet her. She's not going to sprint across the room and climb into your lap on day one. She needs a minute to figure out that she's safe. But once she does? Head bumps. Purring. Lap sitting for hours. She's also litter trained, gets along with other cats she's met in the foster home, and has been great with kids.

If you've got a calm, patient household and maybe another cat who'd appreciate a companion, Bernadette is worth going to meet. She's been through a lot for a one-year-old. She's ready for something quieter and permanent. Mostly Mutts is based in Kennesaw. Reach out to adopt@mostlymutts.org or call to get the process started.
scoring_notes:
• Emotionally rich origin story — stray mom who raised a litter solo — gives readers an instant rooting interest
• Her kittens all found homes while she waited; that contrast creates real urgency and newsletter-ready narrative tension
• Calm, kid-friendly, cat-compatible profile broadens her appeal to a wide swath of East Cobb households

blurb:
Wilson is the kind of dog who drank from the sprayer during his bath and handed out kisses the whole time. He's three years old, about 46 pounds of Bulldog-Boxer mix, and he came to Mostly Mutts from animal control, went through the Prison Pups training program, and is now living in a foster home where he's apparently been a delight. His trainers like him enough that they use him to help teach other dogs how to play. That tells you something.

He's chatty and vocal when he's excited, which is his way of letting you know he's having fun. He loves people, loves other dogs, and has done well with kids of various ages in his foster home. Toddlers are the one exception — he's a big, enthusiastic guy and could accidentally knock a small one over, so older kids are a better fit. He also showed some prey drive toward small animals on walks, so cats are a hard no. But if you have a dog at home who doesn't mind a vocal, enthusiastic playmate, he's worth a look.

He's friendly, goofy, and genuinely happy. Not an anxious dog, not a complicated dog. Just a lot of love in a medium-sized package who hasn't found his people yet.

Mostly Mutts is in Marietta. Visit their website to submit an inquiry and schedule a meet-and-greet.
scoring_notes:
• Sprayer-drinking bath story is immediately shareable and sets an upbeat, fun tone that works well for newsletter readership
• Prison Pups graduate now used as a peer model for other dogs — a credibility signal that makes him stand out from typical shelter profiles
• Dog-friendly, kid-friendly, and enthusiastic personality broadens his appeal, though the no-cats rule and no-toddlers caveat keep him from being a universal fit

blurb:
Glynnis came into Mostly Mutts from animal control, went through their Prison Pups training program, and has been charming every foster home and volunteer she's met since. Her current foster family called her the sweetest dog ever, which is a high bar that she apparently clears without much effort.

She's eight years old, about 41 pounds, and operates in full cuddle mode. She melts into you for scratches, gives out kisses freely, and when she's sleeping soundly, the volunteers say she makes little noises and kicks her feet through whatever she's dreaming about. She's also a solid house dog — alert enough to let you know when someone's at the door, relaxed enough not to make it a whole thing. Her foster noted she does better in a house than an apartment, where the foot traffic and close quarters with other dogs got to be too much for her.

She'd do best as an only dog with no cats in the home. She's done well with kids around 10 and up and genuinely seems to enjoy people once she gets a proper, slow introduction. She's not a complicated dog. She just needs a calm house where she can do her thing, which mostly involves being near you.

Mostly Mutts is in Marietta. Head to their website to submit an inquiry and set up a time to meet her.
scoring_notes:
• Prison Pups graduate who passed through animal control and multiple foster placements — a longer, harder road that makes her adoption feel earned and meaningful
• The sleeping-dog-dream detail is the most visually vivid image in the entire candidate pool and is tailor-made for newsletter copy
• Eight years old with a no-cats, no-dogs requirement narrows her pool significantly, making newsletter exposure genuinely impactful for her chances

blurb:
Eugene has already been somebody's person once. He was adopted, loved for a year, and then his owner had to leave the country and couldn't take him along. That's a rough break for a six-year-old Chihuahua mix who just wants to be near you on the couch. Now he's back at Mostly Mutts, a little stressed about the transition, but slowly settling back in with the help of volunteers he already knows.

He's not a playful, bouncing-off-the-walls kind of dog. He's a lap dog, through and through. He'd rather be curled up next to you than chasing anything around a yard. The volunteers call him a sweet lap dog and a bite-sized bundle of love, which tracks — he's about 17 pounds and mostly wants your attention. He does have some sensitivity around leashing and harnessing, so he needs a patient household that'll give him time to get comfortable at his own pace rather than rushing him.

Eugene does best with adults or older teens who know how to read a dog's signals and give him room to settle in. He's done okay with cats before, and he's not aggressive with other dogs, though he's historically done best as an only dog. If your house is calm and you're not in a rush, he's going to come around.

Mostly Mutts is in Marietta. Visit their website to submit an inquiry and get the meet-and-greet process started.
scoring_notes:
• Owner-surrender after international relocation is the most emotionally resonant backstory in this batch — readers will root for him immediately
• Narrow placement profile (calm adults, no young kids, prefers only-dog home) means he genuinely needs the newsletter's help to find the right match
• Already knows the shelter volunteers, suggesting he's cycled back and been waiting long enough to rebuild trust — quiet urgency worth naming

shelter_name: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue & Adoption, Inc.
blurb:
Turk is JD's littermate over at Mostly Mutts, and if you're already considering JD, here's a thought: why not both? Two kittens at four months old are genuinely easier than one. They burn each other out. They always have someone to play with at 3am so it doesn't have to be you. It's honestly a pretty good deal.

Turk is described as sweet, active, and fun, which at four months old is exactly what you'd expect. He's litter trained, neutered, microchipped, and current on his shots. He's done well with his siblings and would likely be happy in a home with another cat. Kids are welcome as long as they're gentle. Dogs are unknown.

He's a tabby mix, about 3.5 lbs and still growing, so whoever adopts him is going to get a front-row seat to all the chaos and charm that comes with raising a kitten from the small stage. Adoption fee is $175.

Turk is with Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue in Kennesaw. Reach out at adopt@mostlymutts.org or give them a call to arrange a visit.
scoring_notes:
• Bonded-pair angle with JD is a genuine editorial hook — two kittens for one feature, one decision, one fee conversation
• Fully vetted kitten with a low-friction adoption profile makes him easy to recommend to nearly any reader
• No evidence of a long shelter stay; best featured alongside JD rather than as a standalone urgent case

shelter_name: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue & Adoption, Inc.
blurb:
Four months old, 3.5 lbs, and already fully committed to being your best friend. JD is a tabby mix kitten who came into Mostly Mutts as a young stray and has since decided that people are great and toys are better. He's litter trained, already neutered and microchipped, and up to date on his shots. Basically, he's ready to go.

He plays hard and cuddles harder. The listing says his kitten antics will entertain you, and honestly, at four months old with that energy level, that's probably an understatement. If you work from home, expect a coworker who has no respect for your Zoom calls.

He gets along well with his siblings, so if you have another cat at home who'd enjoy a playmate, JD is worth a look. Kids are welcome as long as they're gentle with him. Dogs are unknown. Adoption fee is $175.

JD is with Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue in Kennesaw. Email adopt@mostlymutts.org or call to set up a visit.
scoring_notes:
• Fully vetted, kitten-age, people-loving, and ready to go — lowest barrier to adoption of the entire group
• Work-from-home angle gives readers a relatable, shareable hook that lands well in a community newsletter
• Recent stray arrival with no signs of a long wait; urgency comes from charm, not time served

shelter_name: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue & Adoption, Inc.
blurb:
She was outside on her own at less than a year old, figured out how to survive, and somehow managed to raise a whole litter of kittens while she was at it. That's Bernadette. A young mom who got a second chance when a foster family found her and her babies in their backyard and brought everyone inside. The kittens found homes. Now it's her turn.

She's about a year old, around 7.5 lbs, and her foster describes her as a beautiful cat with a gentle soul. That tracks. She's litter trained, playful, and once she trusts you, she will park herself in your lap and stay there. Head bumps, slow blinks, asking for pets. She warms up on her own timeline, not yours, and that's fine. Give her a few days to feel safe and she'll show you exactly who she is.

She's done well with other cats in her foster home, so if you've already got a cat at home, she could be a good fit. Kids are okay too as long as they're gentle with her. Dogs are unknown.

Bernadette is with Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue, based in Kennesaw. Reach out at adopt@mostlymutts.org or call to get the process started. Adoption fee is $175.
scoring_notes:
• Young survivor-mom whose kittens all found homes — she deserves the same spotlight and the contrast is emotionally compelling
• Gentle, lap-seeking personality with cat-compatible history makes her a realistic fit for many households
• Her kittens moved on while she waits, adding quiet urgency that newsletter readers will feel
